items.item: low sodium tamari or soy sauce
gochujang (Korean red chili paste); check label if gluten free matters
honey (use maple syrup to make it fully vegan)

instructions: Heat the oven to 400 degrees F. Drain the tofu, wrap it in a towel, and press lightly to remove excess liquid.
Cut the tofu into about 1 inch cubes and add to a bowl.
Toss the cubes with the soy sauce, then the cornstarch, then the breadcrumbs, until well coated.
Spread on a parchment-lined baking sheet so the pieces do not touch, and bake 25 minutes, then turn off the oven and let sit 5 more minutes to crisp.
While the tofu bakes, whisk all the sauce ingredients except the 1 teaspoon each of water and cornstarch in a small pot.

Whisk the 1 teaspoon cornstarch with the 1 teaspoon water in a small bowl, stir into the pot, and heat over low/medium, whisking, until the sauce bubbles and thickens. Remove from heat and let it thicken further.
Let the baked tofu cool 5 minutes, then transfer to a bowl and toss with half the sauce, reserving the rest for serving.
Serve over rice with cucumber, carrot, avocado, and sesame seeds; also good with broccoli. Stick with low sodium soy sauce so it does not get too salty.
Air fryer option: cook at 375 degrees F for 15 minutes, shaking every 5 minutes, then toss with the sauce.
leftover_note: Loses its crispness within a few hours, so don't prep the tofu ahead; the sauce can be made ahead and the tofu cooked when ready to serve.
notes: Source page bills it as vegan and gluten free; the listed version uses honey (pareve; swap maple syrup for a fully vegan version) and is gluten free only if GF-certified tamari and breadcrumbs are used.
title: Crispy Gochujang Korean Tofu

tips.title: Vegan swap
tips.text: Use maple syrup instead of honey for a fully vegan version.

tips.title: Gluten-free
tips.text: Use GF-certified tamari and breadcrumbs to keep it gluten free.

tips.title: Extra crispy
tips.text: Press the tofu well and don't crowd the pan — space lets the edges crisp.
